questions.q: What does a Git commit record?
options: Only the files that changed, with no message
A snapshot of the tracked files, a message, the author and time, and its parent commit
A backup copy of your whole computer
A Docker image
questions.explain: Each commit is a save point with a snapshot, a 'why' message, who made it, and a link to the commit before it.

questions.q: You changed 5 files, but only 3 belong in the next commit. What lets you choose?
options: The .git folder
The staging area: git add only those 3
GitHub
git log
questions.explain: Changes move from the working folder to the staging area with git add, and only staged changes go into the commit.

questions.q: What is the difference between a Docker image and a container?
options: They are the same thing
An image is a ready-made package that never changes; a container is a running copy of it
A container is stored on Docker Hub; an image runs on your laptop
An image is a photo of your screen
questions.explain: Like a sealed tiffin and the meal you eat from it. One image can start many separate containers.

questions.q: The first docker run took 3.5 seconds, the second only 0.2 seconds. Why?
options: Your computer warmed up
The first run pulled the image's layers from Docker Hub; the second used the copy already stored
The second run skipped running Python
Docker Hub was faster the second time
questions.explain: Images stay on your computer after the first pull. Starting a container from a local image is very fast.

questions.q: You ran a container without --rm. docker ps shows nothing, but docker ps -a shows it as "Exited (0)". What does that mean?
options: It is still running in secret
It finished successfully and stopped, but was not removed
It crashed
It was never created
questions.explain: docker ps shows only running containers. Exited (0) means the program ended with exit code 0. docker rm removes it; --rm does that automatically.

questions.q: Every docker command says "failed to connect to the docker API ... is the daemon running". What should you do first?
options: Reinstall your operating system
Delete all images
Start Docker Desktop and wait until the Engine is running
Install Python again
questions.explain: The docker command is only a client. It needs the Docker Engine (a background daemon) to be running.

questions.q: Why does this course use python:3.13.18-slim-trixie instead of python:latest?
options: latest is not allowed on Mac
An exact tag gives the same image every time, so every student gets the same result
latest is slower to download
Exact tags are free and latest costs money
questions.explain: latest moves to new images over time without warning. Exact tags (or digests) keep labs reproducible.

questions.q: (Going deeper) On a Mac, uname says Darwin, but inside a container it says Linux. Why?
options: Docker translates Mac programs to Linux
Containers share a Linux kernel, so Docker Desktop runs a small Linux VM and the containers live inside it
The container is broken
uname always lies
questions.explain: Containers are processes that share the kernel of the machine they run on. On Mac and Windows, that machine is Docker Desktop's Linux VM.
